text:
Carolina's win at the United Center was built in a 4:56 stretch of the second period, when three goals turned a 1-0 lead into 4-1. Sebastian Aho scored shorthanded at 2:09, Jackson Blake made it 3-0 at 3:28, and after Roman Kantserov got one back, Taylor Hall's slap shot at 6:05 restored the three-goal cushion. Mark Jankowski had opened the scoring late in the first, and Jordan Martinook added a backhand in the third for 5-1.

The score, for once, was not far from the play. Carolina outshot Chicago 39-26, held a 72-48 edge in shot attempts, and created 3.73 expected goals to 2.65, which gives the Hurricanes a 67 percent chance of winning if every shot were replayed. The second period was the clearest gap, 1.54 to 0.82 in chance quality. Blake finished with a goal and an assist and drove 1.51 expected goals for during his 15:54, with Mike Reilly collecting two assists.

Chicago's best stretch came too late. The third period was nearly even (1.25 to 1.23), and Oliver Moore's goal at 14:14, a 49 percent chance, made it 5-2 but never threatened the result. Spencer Knight allowed five goals on 3.73 expected, about 1.3 goals worse than the shots he faced. Neither team scored on the power play (0-for-2 each), so the game came down to even-strength play, and Carolina controlled it.
